chapter: Dancing schools and Charlie Johnson in New York
title: Playing pop tunes and waltzes for the dancers
summary: Songs had to be kept short; the band played all the popular music, show tunes and waltzes, which made the schools a good training ground.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: tickets, you have a lot of dances. See, then we weren't supposed to play the songs but for so long, you know. "Hey, what are you doing? Cut that song off." We play a song like "Dinah." We'd play it a nice little length and end it, you know.
What were some of the other songs that --
All the pop music. Oh yeah, that's what it had to be. That's what made you -- give you a big name, because you kept up with all the show tunes, all the pop music, all the waltzes. How to play tango.
Oh yeah. Let me tell you. Those schools were good schools for musicians. Young musicians that were coming up that wanted to really learn, you know, how to play and to --
